extra.message: The database password is stored in plaintext in the YAML configuration file that is committed to version control. Anyone with access to the repository can read the database credentials.

The database password 'postgres' is hardcoded in plaintext in the development configuration file. This credential is embedded directly in source-controlled configuration without any external secrets management.
The root logger is configured with logging.DEBUG level, which may cause sensitive information (query data, passwords, session details) to be written to logs.

The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True. This enables verbose error handling that can expose stack traces, source code snippets, environment variables, and internal application state in error responses.

The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True, which enables verbose error messages and debug output that could leak sensitive application internals, stack traces, and configuration details to users.

The csrf_middleware is commented out in the application middleware configuration. This means no Cross-Site Request Forgery protection is active, allowing attackers to trick authenticated users into performing unintended actions.

Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False, meaning all template variables will be rendered without HTML escaping by default. This makes the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks wherever user-controlled data is rendered in templates.

The Student.create method uses Python string formatting (%) to interpolate user-controlled input into the SQL query instead of using proper parameterized queries. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL commands through the 'name' parameter.
The application uses MD5 for password hashing, which is cryptographically broken and susceptible to fast brute-force and rainbow table attacks. MD5 is not suitable for password storage.

User passwords are hashed using MD5, which is a cryptographically broken and extremely fast hash function. MD5 allows attackers to crack passwords at billions of hashes per second using commodity hardware (GPUs).

The RedisStorage is initialized with httponly=False, which means the session cookie is accessible to client-side JavaScript. This makes the session token vulnerable to theft via cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

The RedisStorage is initialized without the secure=True parameter. This means the session cookie will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, making it susceptible to network sniffing and man-in-the-middle attacks.

The handle_40x error handler passes the full exception object (exc) to the 40x error template. Combined with autoescape=False, the template may render exception details including internal attributes, stack frames, and application state.

The handle_50x error handler passes the full exception object (exc) to the 50x error template. Combined with debug=True and autoescape=False, this can expose detailed server-side error information including tracebacks to end users.

The Redis configuration schema in trafaret defines `host`, `port`, and `db` fields but has no `password` field. This makes it impossible to configure Redis authentication through the application configuration.

The Redis configuration schema defines host, port, and db fields but has no password field. As a result, Redis is connected to without any authentication (no AUTH command), allowing anyone who can reach the Redis port to access all data including session tokens.
The database password is embedded directly in the connection string (DSN) in plaintext. If an attacker gains access to the application's memory or logs, they can extract the database credentials.

The Redis connection is established without any password or authentication configuration. If Redis is exposed (even within the Docker network), an attacker could connect to it directly and access session data, including session tokens.

The auth_user_processor retrieves the full User NamedTuple (which includes the pwd_hash field) and passes it as 'auth_user' to every template's context. Any template rendering {{ auth_user.pwd_hash }} would leak the MD5 password hash to users. Additionally, if an attacker can inject into templates (via XSS or other means), they can read the hash.
The login handler (index POST) has no rate limiting, account lockout, failed attempt counter, CAPTCHA, or exponential backoff. An attacker can brute-force usernames and passwords without restriction.

After successful authentication (user.check_password returns True), the session['user_id'] is set but the session ID is never regenerated via session.regenerate() or equivalent. This allows an attacker to fixate a session ID, trick the victim into authenticating with it, and then hijack the authenticated session.
The students endpoint POST handler creates new student records with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can add students to the system.
The POST handler for /students/ creates a new student record without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can create students in the database.
The students POST handler does not validate input against STUDENT_SCHEMA before calling Student.create. A missing 'name' key would cause an unhandled KeyError exception.
The GET branch of the students handler returns all student records with no authentication check. Any visitor can enumerate all students in the system.
The student detail handler returns a specific student's profile and all their marks with no authentication check. Any visitor can view any student's grades by ID.
The courses endpoint POST handler creates new course records with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can add courses to the system.
The `courses` view handler has no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can list all courses (GET) and create new courses (POST).
The courses handler accepts POST requests to create new course records with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated visitor can create arbitrary course records.
The POST handler for /courses/ creates a new course record without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can create courses in the database.
The courses POST handler does not validate input against COURSE_SCHEMA before calling Course.create. Missing keys would cause unhandled KeyError exceptions.
The GET branch of the courses handler returns all course records with no authentication check. Any visitor can enumerate all courses.
The course detail handler returns course details, reviews (which may contain XSS), and all students with no authentication check.
The `review` view handler has no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can POST to create course reviews.
The review endpoint POST handler creates course reviews with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can submit reviews for any course.
The POST handler for creating reviews on courses has no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can post reviews containing arbitrary text.
The evaluate handler accepts POST requests to create grade marks for any student/course combination with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated visitor can assign grades to any student.

The `evaluate` handler (POST-only) that creates grade/marks for students has no authentication or authorization check. Unlike `logout` which has `@authorize()`, this handler is completely unguarded. Any unauthenticated user can evaluate any student in any course.

The evaluate endpoint (POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id}) creates student marks/grades with no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can assign grades to any student in any course.
The evaluate handler that creates marks for students has no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can assign grades to any student for any course.
